text: Experiments were conducted on cats under ketamine anesthesia; a study was made of pulse activity of bulbar respiratory neurons, electrical activity of the diaphragm and of the intercostal muscles; pO2, pCO2, pH, and arterial blood oxygen saturation were determined in combination with hypoxia and hypercapnia. When hypoxic gas mixtures were administered for respiration, the developing hypocapnia disrupted the rhythmic activity of the respiratory neurons, causing them to exhibit a pathological Cheyne-Stokes pattern. After adding 2% CO2 to the hypoxic gas mixtures, the gaseous composition of the arterial blood returned to its initial state; this addition prevented the development of hypercapnia and disruptions in the rhythmic discharge activity of the respiratory neurons. Adding 5% CO2 to the hypoxic gas mixtures resulted in a negative impact: initially, it intensified and then depressed the pulse activity of the respiratory neurons, leading to metabolic and respiratory acidosis, and promoting asphyxia.
